Reactivity
A major nutritional concern of molybdenum is its ability to antagonize copper. Indiscriminant spraying of soils with molybdenum
has been shown to affect the growth and productivity of ruminants. The effect relates to the formation of thiomolybdates in the
rumen. The thiomolybdates interact and bind copper preventing its absorption from the rumen. Thiomolybdates have a very
high afﬁnity for copper almost to the exclusion of other metal ions. Lately, thiomolybdates have been used to control copper toxicity
in Wilson's disease, a genetic disease of copper poisoning in humans.
Nickel
